base_properties.human_readable: GHQ Drafting as Hybrid Authorship (Japanese Liberal Insertion Reading)

perspectives.label: Japanese Occupied Population Under Duress
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 1: OCCUPIED POPULATION (SNARE) — The Diet members who 'amended' the constitution faced explicit GHQ authority and implicit threat of continued occupation. They negotiated within a radically constrained choice set. Even if amendments occurred, the foundational text was drafted without their participation and imposed under occupation law. Maximum extraction from the population's structural position: they ratified a document whose core frame was alien-authored, even if they inserted social rights provisions. No exit option exists from the occupation context; any voting was constrained choice.

perspectives.label: Japanese Liberal Drafters Within GHQ Process
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 2: JAPANESE LIBERAL INTELLECTUALS (ROPE) — The Japanese liberal intellectuals who participated in the drafting process experienced genuine coordination: they had substantive input on Article 25 (social rights), they shaped the revision discussions in the Diet, they secured amendments to GHQ's initial proposals. Their exit was constrained (cooperation or exclusion from the process), but within the process they achieved real coordination outcomes. This perspective sees the constraint as a problem they solved — converting an alien-authored framework into a co-authored document. Moderate experienced extraction because they paid the cost of occupancy but gained strategic input.

perspectives.label: GHQ Supreme Command Authority
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 3: GHQ SUPREME COMMAND (TANGLED ROPE) — The occupation authority needed Japanese cooperation to make the constitution stick: a purely imposed document would face legitimacy deficits and resistance. GHQ benefited from Japanese liberal input (it provided local buy-in and legal sophistication); it also extracted through structural authority (the final veto remained GHQ's, time was compressed to 6 days, the English-language first draft was a GHQ product). GHQ experienced the constraint as solving a coordination problem (how to make foreign governance locally acceptable) while maintaining extraction (the constitution remained subordinate to occupation law). Arbitrage exit: GHQ could have reverted to military rule if the constitutional path failed.

perspectives.label: Historical Scholarship (Hybrid Authorship Evidence)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 4: HISTORICAL SCHOLARSHIP / ANALYTICAL (ROPE) — The scholarly record (Koseki Shoichi, Dower, local Japanese historians) establishes that Japanese intellectuals made substantive contributions: Article 25 (social rights minimum standard), the pacifist Article 9's specific framing, amendments to GHQ's property rights provisions. The analytical observer sees coordination that worked — the hybrid authorship narrative is supported by archival evidence, Diet records, and GHQ's own acknowledgment of Japanese input. This perspective experiences no extraction — the coordination mechanism is transparent and the scholarly documentation is robust.

perspectives.label: Constitutional Legitimacy Theater
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 5: CONSTITUTIONAL LEGITIMACY MAINTENANCE (PITON) — The hybrid authorship narrative serves a purely performative function in contemporary Japanese jurisprudence: it maintains the fiction that the constitution is legitimate (not merely imposed) while the actual legal enforcement remains unchanged. Courts cite the Diet's amendments to Article 25 to defend the constitution's legitimacy, but the substantive content would be identical whether the narrative was 'hybrid authorship' or 'pure imposition.' The theater is high (0.35-0.45): the narrative performs legitimacy work without changing doctrine. The constraint persists through institutional inertia — the constitution is treated as domestically authored even though the alternative (acknowledging imposition) would not change its legal force.

perspectives.label: Constitutional Revision Movement
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 6: CONSTITUTIONAL REVISION ADVOCATES (SCAFFOLD) — Organized actors pushing for revision (conservative politicians, Article 9 critics, sovereignty advocates) see the hybrid authorship reading as a temporary scaffold supporting a foreign-imposed frame. By claiming Japanese authorship, the scaffold maintains the status quo and delays the structural reckoning with occupation. Revision advocates experience the constraint as enforced stability — the hybrid authorship narrative suppresses pressure for rewriting. The sunset clause is implicit: if/when constitutional revision succeeds, the hybrid narrative becomes moot and the scaffold dissolves. Constrained exit because revision is politically difficult but not impossible.

perspectives.label: Logical Analysis of Authorship Determinacy
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 7: ANALYTICAL OBSERVER (FALSE SUMMIT CANDIDATE) — From a civilizational/universal perspective, the authorship question may appear as an immutable logical fact: either the constitution was imposed or it was co-authored, and historical records are either clear or irreducibly ambiguous. This perspective treats the question as a matter of fact whose answer is discoverable and settled. However, the structural data contradicts the mountain classification — the authorship narrative functions to legitimize or delegitimize the constitution's authority, and competing narratives serve different institutional interests. The 'immutability' is a false summit: it naturalizes a narrative choice (which authorship story to emphasize) as a discoverable fact.

omegas.question: What threshold of input — draft revision, amendment proposal, substantive reframing — constitutes co-authorship rather than mere consultation?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparative analysis across constitutional drafting processes; examination of GHQ's counterfactual revisions (what would the constitution have been without Japanese input); archival tracing of each Article's provenance
omegas.impact: High threshold (structural authorship requires top-level framing): hybrid authorship claim is weakened; closer to pure imposition. Low threshold (any substantive amendment counts): hybrid authorship claim is strengthened; moves toward genuine co-authorship. Different thresholds produce different ε values and different beneficiary/victim maps.

omegas.question: Can meaningful co-authorship exist when one party negotiates under duress, with exit blocked and time compressed to 6 days?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparative analysis of other constitutions drafted under occupation (Germany 1919, Iraq 2005, Afghanistan 2004); determination of whether duress-constrained input counts as genuine authorship or as strategic accommodation within coercion
omegas.impact: If duress negates co-authorship claim: hybrid reading collapses into imposed-constitution critique. If duress-constrained input still counts as authorship: hybrid reading is sustained. The answer depends on whether 'authorship' requires voluntariness or only requires substantive influence.
omegas.description: Whether negotiation under duress constitutes genuine co-authorship

omegas.question: Does the hybrid authorship narrative suppress the pure-imposition critique by misdescribing the occupation context, or does it accurately capture a real dimension of the drafting process that the pure-imposition reading ignores?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Textual analysis of how each narrative frames the same evidence (Diet amendments, Article 25 insertion, GHQ's retained veto); identification of evidence each narrative suppresses or emphasizes; examination of institutional interests served by each framing
omegas.impact: If the hybrid narrative instrumentalizes to suppress critique: extractiveness rises (suppression is active misdescription). If the hybrid narrative captures genuine bilateral process: extractiveness stays moderate (the narrative is truthful even if selective). The distinction determines whether this constraint is Snare, Tangled Rope, or Rope.
omegas.description: Whether the co-authorship narrative is truthful or instrumentally suppressive

omegas.question: Do the hybrid authorship reading and the pure-imposition critique logically foreclose each other, or can both remain coherent within a single interpretive framework that emphasizes different aspects of the same events?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Formal logical analysis: if the hybrid reading is true (Japanese liberals made substantive contributions), does this make the imposition critique false? If both can be simultaneously true (there was both genuine Japanese input AND genuine occupation duress), the readings coexist rather than foreclose.
omegas.impact: If foreclosure: this reading and the imposition critique are competing singulars, and only one can be valid (Ω_C computation routes to foreclosure gates). If coexistence: both readings are live, and the constitutional contest operates via different emphasizing factions (network contamination, not logical inconsistency).
omegas.description: Whether hybrid authorship and imposition readings logically foreclose or coexist

commentary.narrative_context: This story instantiates ONE READING of a contested constitutional kernel: the question of who authored Japan's postwar constitution. The kernel is the 1947 Constitution itself — a stabilized, formalizable text that different historical and political factions interpret as either imposed-from-outside, co-authored-by-Japanese-liberals, or embraced-by-the-people-over-seven-decades. The HYBRID AUTHORSHIP READING (this story) claims that Japanese liberal intellectuals made substantive contributions to the drafting: Article 25's social rights minimum were a Japanese insertion, the Diet amended GHQ's initial proposals, and the constitutional process was a negotiation, not a dictation. This reading suppresses the pure-imposition narrative by demonstrating that Japanese actors shaped the document. It also differs from the embraced-revolution reading, which accepts the constitution as legitimate because the people chose not to amend it over 77 years—a choice-based legitimacy rather than authorship-based legitimacy. The hybrid authorship reading operates on the constraint level: it claims legitimacy from the drafting process itself (Japanese participation), whereas the embraced-revolution reading claims legitimacy from post-ratification durability (sustained unamended choice). The extractiveness value (0.38) reflects that the hybrid narrative provides genuine coordination (Japanese liberals did make substantive input) but also active suppression (the occupation duress context is backgrounded). The suppression trajectory shows decline over time (0.68→0.42) as archival evidence accumulates and the historical record becomes harder to dispute—the constraint weakens as the narrative's empirical basis becomes undeniable.
key_agents: Japanese Liberal Intellectuals (Yoshida Shigeru, Suzuki Yasuzo, constitutional scholars): moderate power, constrained exit — negotiated substantive input within GHQ's authority framework; beneficiaries of the hybrid authorship narrative because it credits their participation

GHQ Supreme Command (SCAP, Douglas MacArthur's administrative structure): institutional power, arbitrage exit — needed Japanese cooperation for constitutional legitimacy; beneficiary of coordination that made the occupation document locally acceptable

Japanese Diet Members: moderate-to-powerless power (under occupation), trapped exit — ratified the constitution under duress; victims of the extraction of constitutional authority, beneficiaries of Article 25 insertions

Pure-Imposition Narrative Advocates: institutional power (revisionists, sovereignty advocates), constrained exit — the hybrid authorship reading suppresses their core claim (that occupation negates legitimacy); they are victims of the narrative that obscures duress

Embraced-Revolution Narrative Advocates: institutional power (constitutional defenders, status-quo maintainers), arbitrage exit — coexist with hybrid authorship reading but emphasize different legitimacy source (sustained choice vs. authorship); neither forecloses the other

Contemporary Historiography Community: analytical power, analytical exit — the hybrid authorship reading's primary evidence base; beneficiary of detailed archival work that establishes Japanese input; analyst position that transcends occupation-era constraints
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness (0.38): Moderate. The hybrid authorship narrative provides genuine coordination value — Japanese liberals did shape the document, Article 25 is documented as a Japanese insertion, the Diet's amendments are recorded. The narrative truthfully describes substantive Japanese participation. However, extractiveness is not low because the narrative also suppresses the occupation context: it emphasizes Japanese agency while backgrounding the duress, time compression, and GHQ's retained veto authority. The extraction lies in the emphasis and framing, not in fabrication. The trajectory (0.48→0.38 over 50 years) reflects the constraint's weakening: as archival evidence accumulates, the historical record becomes harder to dispute, and the extraction mechanism (selective emphasis) loses force. Suppression (0.42, declining from 0.68): The occupation duress is not erased but is systematized into background context. Early suppression is high because the occupation's immediate coercive power is vivid; suppression declines over time as the occupation recedes into history and becomes deniable only by explicit distortion. Theater ratio (0.35, rising slightly): The hybrid authorship narrative has moderate performative content. It performs legitimacy work (the constitution is not merely imposed) without changing the legal content or constitutional doctrine. The slight rise (0.25→0.38) reflects increasing ritualization: the narrative becomes embedded in constitutional jurisprudence and educational materials, functioning primarily as legitimacy theater rather than as a contested historical claim. Claimed type is Tangled Rope because the constraint combines genuine coordination (Japanese intellectual input) with asymmetric extraction (the occupation's retained authority, the backgrounding of duress). GHQ benefited from both: the coordination mechanism (local buy-in) and the extraction mechanism (occupation authority remained supreme). Japanese intellectuals benefited from the coordination (they shaped the document) but bore extraction costs (they negotiated under duress, their amendments occurred only on GHQ's sufferance).
commentary.perspectival_gap: The perspectival gap is the core of this constraint. The occupied population under duress sees the constitution as pure extraction (Snare) — they ratified an alien-authored document. The Japanese liberal intellectuals who participated see genuine coordination (Rope) — they solved a real problem (making occupation rule legitimate) and secured substantive input. GHQ sees a hybrid (Tangled Rope) — it needed Japanese cooperation (coordination) but maintained structural authority (extraction). The revision advocates see a temporary scaffold — the hybrid narrative maintains constitutional stability that revision would disrupt. The analytical observer risks seeing an immutable fact (Mountain: either it was imposed or it was co-authored) but this is a false summit: the authorship question is not a discoverable fact but a narrative choice that serves institutional interests. The historiography community sees the process transparently (Rope, analytical view) — the evidence is clear, the narrative is truthful, there is no remaining dispute.
commentary.directionality_logic: Directionality (d) flows from the structural position of each agent relative to this constraint. Japanese intellectuals who participated are moderate-powered agents with constrained exit; they benefited from the coordination outcome (shaped the document) but paid the cost of occupation duress (negotiation under authority, not freely). Their derived d is approximately 0.45 (both beneficiary and victim, constrained exit). GHQ is an institutional beneficiary with arbitrage exit (could have reverted to military rule); their d is approximately 0.15 (beneficiary with high exit optionality). The Diet members under occupation are powerless agents with trapped exit; their d is approximately 0.95 (full target, no exit). The analytical historian has no structural stake in the constraint; their d is approximately 0.72 (observer position). The f(d) sigmoid transforms these d values to experienced extractiveness. Beneficiaries with arbitrage exit experience negative or very low chi (they control the frame and can exit if dissatisfied). Trapped agents experience high chi (they bore extraction costs without choice). Constrained beneficiary-victims experience moderate chi (they paid costs but gained outcomes).
commentary.kernel_context: KERNEL: ghq_drafting_imposition — The contested text is the 1947 Japanese Constitution. The kernel is fixed and formalized (the Constitution itself is the stable reference). Different political and historical factions read this kernel as imposing occupation rule (pure-imposition reading), as co-authored by Japanese liberals (hybrid authorship reading, THIS STORY), or as embraced by popular choice over seven decades (embraced-revolution reading). READING: hybrid_authorship_reading — This reading instantiates the claim that Japanese liberal intellectuals made substantive contributions to the drafting, that Article 25's social rights are a Japanese insertion, and that the Diet amended GHQ's proposals. This reading's authority-grounding is 'lineage' (it appeals to a chain of transmission from the constitutional scholars who participated, through archival evidence, to contemporary historiography). Its kernel-codification is 'formalized' (the Constitution is a written fixed text). SIBLING READINGS: (1) embraced_revolution_reading — legitimacy from sustained non-amendment over 77 years; (2) imposed_constitution_critique — legitimacy requires revision because the constitution was drafted by foreigners in English under duress. These siblings are NOT this story; they are separate constraint narratives. EXPECTED STRUCTURAL DELTA: The hybrid authorship narrative suppresses the pure-imposition claim (extraction mechanism: emphasis on Japanese agency while backgrounding duress). The beneficiary is the historiographical community and the Japanese liberal participants (they are credited with authorship). The victim set is both purity narratives: the pure-imposition reading is suppressed (its duress emphasis is backgrounded), and the embraced-revolution reading is displaced as the primary legitimacy source (authorship-based legitimacy competes with choice-based legitimacy). The extractiveness is moderate (0.38) and shared unevenly: GHQ extracted maximum authority (occupation remained supreme), Japanese intellectuals extracted moderate benefits (shaped the document but under duress), the population extracted procedural legitimacy (the constitution bore marks of Japanese input) but under coercive conditions.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: KERNEL READING MANDATROPHY: The hybrid authorship reading avoids the mandatrophy by routing it to the omega variables rather than trying to claim single-valued classification. The core mandatrophy is: 'Is this constraint pure coordination (the Japanese drafting contribution was real and beneficial) or pure extraction (the occupation authority remained supreme and the negotiation occurred under duress)?' The reading resolves this by declaring Tangled Rope — both coordination AND extraction are present. Japanese intellectuals gained genuine input (coordination achieved) but paid the cost of occupation duress (extraction occurred). GHQ gained cooperation and legitimacy (coordination benefit) while maintaining authority (extraction mechanism). The constraint is not a misclassification of one type as another; it is a genuinely hybrid mechanism. The mandatrophy is resolved by the perspectival gate: from the occupied population's view (Snare), from the Japanese participants' view (Rope), from GHQ's view (Tangled Rope), from the analytical view (Rope with false-summit risk). Each perspective is valid; no perspective is the 'true' one. The constraint's classification depends on the observer's structural position relative to the occupation framework.

network.dual_formulation_note: The GHQ drafting imposition constraint decomposes into three structurally distinct readings: (1) hybrid_authorship_reading (this story, ε=0.38) — Japanese liberals made substantive contributions, coordination with extraction; (2) embraced_revolution_reading (separate story, ε=0.22 estimated) — legitimacy from 77 years of sustained choice, Rope classification; (3) imposed_constitution_critique (separate story, ε=0.64 estimated) — occupation duress negates legitimacy, demands revision, Snare classification. Each reading has its own beneficiary/victim structure, its own suppression mechanism, and its own ε value. All three are linked via network.affects_constraints because they are competing readings of the same constitutional kernel. The ε values differ because each reading uses different observables: hybrid authorship uses the archive of Japanese amendments as the measuring basis; embraced revolution uses the 77-year non-amendment trajectory; imposed critique uses the occupation law framework as the measuring basis. Per the ε-invariance principle, different observables → different constraints. All three exist simultaneously as live positions held by different institutional and political factions.
